This kind of tight integration between API and hardware is completely the norm in consoles. It's not something exciting. This is the kind of thing a console manufacturer wouldn't normally talk about, because it's a no-brainer to have an integrated architecture.

Corporate hype is ridiculous these days. In the case of DX12, you get a lot of buzzwords and conflation of a multitude of disaparate ideas. DX12 is technically a win on PC because PC graphics APIs were missing an obvious draw call optimization on PC, and Mantle was created to alleviate that (resulting in Vulkan and DX12 solving the same problem as well as bringing a few other improvements along the same lines). By and large this was not a particular problem on consoles. It's just that a custom design has to be made whenever you make a console, and naturally DX12 is what they're going to use. The extent to which it'll reduce the amount of draw calls is likely to be marginal on consoles - it would actually be shocking if a console didn't have a custom batching scheme in the first place!

Let's look at some of the wording:

Our implementation of D3D12 supports all Xbox Ones, and games have already shipped that use it. When a game using D3D12 starts up, we reprogram the GPU's Command Processor front-end. The 50 per cent CPU rendering overhead improvement was reported by shipping games. The amount of win is dependent on the game engine and content, and not all games will see that size of improvement.

• DX12 can actually run everywhere, including xbone, should be no surprise except MS intentionally doesn't support it on PC unless you're on win10

• Up to 50% CPU rendering overhead improvement reported: this is an improvement in the CPU rendering overhead. This is NOT a general 50% CPU improvement, the CPU does a lot more than push draw calls. And you'll get 0 effective improvement if the bottleneck isn't the CPU, or is a CPU process other than draw calls (and I'd argue most games should be GPU limited, and if they aren't, they'll likely be limited by another CPU process such as AI and game scripts).

What is commonly implied by MS marketing is some kind of similar gain as DirectX 12™ on PC in an area where consoles shouldn't really have a huge problem. That's definitely not the case, and MS knows it but they're benefiting from being vague. The guy who submitted that update I quoted in my previous post is more honest and gives a more realistic outlook than others at MS who've made claims.
